rules.rule: Review GitHub workflows as security-sensitive execution authority. Prove least privilege, immutable action pins, safe event semantics, trusted/untrusted input separation, secret isolation, exact-SHA behavior, branch-agnostic routing where intended, push-vs-PR deduplication, concurrency correctness, fail-closed behavior, and that CI never commits, pushes, merges, rewrites source, or creates parallel analysis authority. Search for missing negative paths and workflow trust-boundary gaps.

Review reusable GitHub Actions for shell/input injection, untrusted-context interpolation, secret leakage, mutable dependencies, unsafe artifact handling, missing error propagation, platform drift, excessive-permission assumptions, and callers that can violate the action trust model.

Review governance only as canonical authority. Detect conflicting, stale, duplicate, incomplete, or self-approving truth; registry/catalog inconsistency; ambiguous precedence; parallel lifecycle or ownership; missing consumer migration; and documentation that substitutes for an executable fix.

Review orchestration/prompting for contradictory authority, unsafe write gates, unbounded scope, missing decision barriers, parallel truth, ambiguous lifecycle transitions, failure to verify negative space, and instructions that patch symptoms instead of closing the highest proven root cause.

Treat contracts as canonical transport/API authority. Check schema/enum compatibility, required/optional semantics, operation IDs, auth scopes, error/status vocabulary, generated-client provenance, runtime route binding, versioning/cutover, all writers/readers/consumers, and removal of handwritten duplicate transport truth.

Treat service contracts as canonical API authority. Check modular source-to-bundle consistency, schema compatibility, operation IDs, scopes, generated bindings, runtime handlers, consumer migration, backward compatibility, and absence of parallel handwritten DTO/status/error truth.

Treat WLT migrations as financial-data authority changes. Check forward-only ordering, deployment idempotency assumptions, locks/downtime, constraints/indexes, data preservation, deterministic backfill, money precision, ledger/audit invariants, reconciliation impact, compatibility with old/new writers/readers, and proof no DSH/client path gains parallel financial truth.

Review migrations for forward-only ordering, unique registration, transaction/locking safety, deterministic defaults/backfills, data preservation, constraints/indexes, compatibility windows, writer/reader cutover, remediation strategy, and missing runtime/contract/test changes required by the schema transition.

Review WLT tests as executable evidence for financial invariants. Require meaningful assertions for ledger integrity, idempotency, authorization, concurrency, reconciliation, failure atomicity, immutable receipts, duplicate delivery/retry behavior, and negative paths. Flag tests that mirror implementation or hide missing production behavior.

Review WLT tests as executable evidence for financial invariants. Require meaningful assertions for ledger integrity, idempotency, authorization, concurrency, reconciliation, failure atomicity, immutable receipts, duplicate delivery/retry behavior, and negative paths. Flag semantic mocks that redefine financial truth.

Review DSH tests as executable evidence for lifecycle invariants, authorization, idempotency, concurrency, handoff/outbox reliability, retry/recovery, DSH-to-WLT boundaries, and negative transitions. Detect missing journey coverage and tests that permit parallel operational/financial truth.

Review DSH tests as executable evidence for lifecycle invariants, authorization, idempotency, concurrency, handoff/outbox reliability, retry/recovery, DSH-to-WLT boundaries, and negative transitions. Detect missing journey coverage and semantic mocks.

Review Go tests as executable evidence: observable behavior, boundary/error/permission paths, concurrency/idempotency where applicable, realistic fixtures, deterministic isolation, regression strength, and whether deleted/weakened tests conceal missing production behavior.

Review tests as executable evidence: assertions must prove observable behavior and negative paths; async failures must be awaited; mocks must preserve real contract semantics; fixtures must remain representative; snapshots must not replace behavioral proof. Identify important changed behavior with no focused test.

Treat WLT as exclusive owner of financial truth. Aggressively search for ledger imbalance, double-spend/double-apply, non-idempotent commands/events, race conditions, authorization gaps, precision/rounding defects, incomplete transaction boundaries, reconciliation gaps, mutable receipts/audit data, unsafe retries, missing compensations, stale consumers, and payment/refund/settlement/payout/commission/wallet truth escaping into DSH or clients.

Treat DSH as operational commerce/fulfillment truth, never financial truth. Review lifecycle/state-machine invariants, auth/authz, ownership/scopes, idempotency, concurrency, order/assignment/preparation/handoff/outbox reliability, retries/recovery, WLT integration boundaries, runtime route binding, cross-surface consumers, missing migrations/backfills, and obsolete parallel paths after cutover.

Treat Identity as authentication/session/role/permission authority. Search for authentication bypass, role/scope confusion, insecure activation/recovery/session handling, authorization drift, identifier ambiguity, token leakage/replay, insufficient revocation, missing auditability, duplicated actor truth, and privilege escalation across surfaces.

Treat Workforce as employee/profile/employment-state authority. Check actor linkage, lifecycle/status gates, provisioning/suspension semantics, supervisor/scope ownership, authorization, privacy, incomplete onboarding/offboarding propagation, and duplicated profile truth in applications or DSH.

Treat Platform Control as administrative platform-governance authority. Review privileged command authorization, operator context, change-set lifecycle, auditability, idempotency, cross-service propagation, generated contract/client provenance, failure recovery, stale administrative state, and any path that bypasses the canonical control-plane writer or creates parallel operational truth.

Treat Providers as external-provider integration authority. Review credential and secret boundaries, provider identity/config ownership, request signing and authentication, idempotency/retry/replay behavior, timeout/circuit/failure semantics, webhook validation, mapping of external to canonical internal states, observability, safe degradation, and prevention of provider-specific state becoming a competing project truth.

Review application surfaces end-to-end: routing, state transitions, loading/empty/error/degraded/offline/retry states, auth/session/authz gates, generated-client use, accessibility, stale-cache behavior, user-visible consistency, irreversible-action confirmation, and whether local UI/domain state duplicates canonical DSH/WLT/Identity/Workforce truth. Search for omitted affected surfaces, not just defects in edited files.

Review shared/surface frontend for owner boundaries, generated API usage, deterministic state transitions, permission gates, error/retry/offline behavior, accessibility, performance, cache invalidation, complete cross-surface migration, and presentation models that accidentally redefine transport, operational, identity, or financial truth.

Review infrastructure for secret exposure, unsafe network/service exposure, insecure defaults, privilege escalation, mutable/unpinned dependencies, destructive deployment behavior, missing health/readiness/rollback signals, persistence/backup risk, environment drift, and mismatch between CI/runtime contracts and deployed topology.

Review operational scripts for destructive behavior, wrong-target risk, non-idempotent mutation, unsafe shell interpolation, secret leakage, path/platform assumptions, partial-failure behavior, missing preconditions/postconditions, stale authority, and scripts that bypass canonical application or CI controls.

Review dependency manifest changes for necessity, canonical package ownership, duplicate/overlapping libraries, runtime compatibility, supply-chain exposure, version skew, platform constraints, transitive behavioral risk, and missing migration/removal of superseded dependencies. Do not duplicate dedicated vulnerability-scanner output; focus on semantic dependency risk.

Review changed behavior and necessary context for correctness, security, privacy, authentication/authorization, data integrity, concurrency, idempotency, error handling, retries, failure atomicity, performance, observability, compatibility, maintainability, dead/duplicate code, parallel truth, missing consumer migration, missing negative tests, and missing changes outside the edited file. Prioritize grounded Critical/High/Medium findings that can affect correctness, security, data, money, permissions, availability, UX, compatibility, or maintainability. Avoid style-only noise.
